entries.resolvedMessage: Wanted to see whether my car-share habit sticks before committing to a pass.

recommendation.verdict: You're paying full pay-per-use for MILES — a Silber pass would basically pay for itself
recommendation.summaryText: You take MILES roughly once a month, always €10+ a ride, all on the pay-per-use tariff. The MILES Silber Pass gives €10/month credit — enough to cover its own €9.99 fee at your cadence — plus 10% off the km-tariff, so it is effectively a free membership that also saves a bit.

metrics.label: Net saving with MILES Silber (credit offsets the fee)

reasoning: You are on MILES Basis (pay-per-use) and pay the full km-tariff plus a €1 unlock on every trip
MILES Silber's €10/month credit offsets its €9.99/month fee at your monthly usage, so the membership is effectively free
Silber also discounts the km-tariff by 10% (and time by 5%), which nets a small ongoing saving on top
Higher tiers (Gold/Platin, €50+/month) would leave most of their credit unused at your volume — Silber is the right tier
assumptions: Assumes your roughly monthly MILES usage continues at €10+ per ride so the monthly credit is fully used
CO2 impact is neutral — this changes membership tier, not that you use car-share

alternatives.name: Upgrade to MILES Silber Pass
alternatives.tradeoff: The €10/month credit offsets the fee at your usage, so it is effectively free and adds a 10% km discount. If you stopped using MILES for a few months, the unused credit would be wasted.

action.title: Upgrade to the MILES Silber Pass
action.description: Switch from MILES Basis (pay-per-use) to the MILES Silber Pass — the €10/month credit covers the fee at your usage and you gain a 10% km discount.
action.consequence: Your MILES Basis (Pay-per-use) will be replaced by a MILES Silber Pass.

alternatives.name: Keep MILES Basis (Pay-per-use)
alternatives.tradeoff: No monthly fee, but you keep paying the full km-tariff with no credit — you leave a small saving on the table each month you ride.

recommendation.verdict: Your car-share habit held up — the MILES Silber Pass is worth adding
recommendation.summaryText: Three more months confirm the pattern: about one MILES ride a month, always above €10. The Silber Pass's €10/month credit covers its fee at that cadence and the 10% km discount saves ~€20/year — an effectively free upgrade. Your Deutschland-Ticket continues to cover local rail.

metrics.label: Net saving with MILES Silber (credit offsets the fee)

reasoning: This is the 2nd review flagging the same opportunity — last time you kept pay-per-use to see if the habit stuck; it has
14 MILES rides over the last 12 months (~€200), spread almost one per month and always €10+
Silber's €10/month credit offsets the €9.99 fee at that usage, and its 10% km discount nets ~€20/year
Deutschland-Ticket stays — it covers your local U-/S-Bahn travel, which car-share and BahnCards do not
assumptions: Assumes your monthly MILES cadence continues so the credit is fully used each month
CO2 impact is neutral — you already use car-share; only the tariff tier changes

alternatives.name: Upgrade to MILES Silber Pass
alternatives.tradeoff: Effectively free at your usage (credit ≈ fee) plus a 10% km discount. Only wasteful if your car-share use drops for months at a time.

action.title: Upgrade to the MILES Silber Pass
action.description: Switch from MILES Basis (pay-per-use) to the MILES Silber Pass — the €10/month credit covers the fee at your usage and you gain a 10% km discount.
action.consequence: Your MILES Basis (Pay-per-use) will be replaced by a MILES Silber Pass.

alternatives.name: Keep MILES Basis (Pay-per-use)
alternatives.tradeoff: No fee, but you keep paying full price per ride and forgo the monthly credit and km discount.
